decisions.reason: Bosch 62825 is unscoped while the article specifies different OEM and tuned-car injector numbers and requires diagnostic selection and coding.

sourceEvidence.title: Direct Fuel Injector Failure (S55)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace failed injectors with OEM updated version (BMW 13538616079, ~$80-$120/each). For tuned cars making higher boost, 1200cc S63TU-spec Bosch injectors (13647599876 / BOS-0261500136, ~$150-$200/each) provide 33% more fuel flow. Injector coding/adaptation via BMW diagnostic software is required after replacement. Professional installation $400-$800 for complete set.

decisions.reason: The unscoped Bosch 62825 claim does not prove the S55 injector index/application or the article's six-injector repair requirements.

sourceEvidence.title: S55 High-Pressure Fuel Injector Failure - F82/F83 M4
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace all 6 injectors together to prevent repeat repairs. Perform walnut blast carbon cleaning on intake valves while injectors are removed (labor overlap saves $400-600). Use Top Tier gasoline to minimize carbon buildup. Add fuel system cleaner (Liqui Moly Valve Clean) every 5,000 miles to reduce carbon deposits. BMW parts are expensive; some shops use OEM Bosch injectors at lower cost. Labor is 4-6 hours for injector replacement.

decisions.reason: The article primarily prescribes the oil-filter-housing gasket and makes the oil-cooler gasket conditional; the current claim is unscoped across N20 and B48.

sourceEvidence.title: Oil Filter Housing Gasket Leak
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the oil filter housing gasket and clean all affected surfaces. Also inspect and replace the oil cooler gasket if present. Use only OEM-quality gaskets as aftermarket gaskets tend to fail prematurely. Typical repair takes 2-3 hours.

decisions.reason: DEP1038 is unscoped across a sixteen-year, multi-engine article and omits the separately prescribed thermostat.

sourceEvidence.title: Electric Water Pump Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the electric water pump and thermostat together, as they are part of the same cooling circuit and the thermostat often fails concurrently. Bleed the cooling system thoroughly after replacement. Some owners carry a spare pump due to the sudden failure nature.

decisions.reason: VS50711 is unscoped across M54 and N52 applications and does not cover the article's additional VANOS O-ring branch.

sourceEvidence.title: Valve Cover Gasket Oil Leaks (M54, N52 Engines)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace valve cover gasket and VANOS solenoid o-rings ($300-500 independent shop, $700-1,000 dealer, $80-150 DIY parts). On M54 engines, also replace ignition coil boots if contaminated by oil ($50 additional). Use OEM BMW gasket or Victor Reinz brand - aftermarket quality matters for long-term seal. Relatively straightforward DIY repair - saves $200-400 in labor. YouTube and Bimmerfest have detailed model-specific guides. Monitor oil level weekly and top off as needed (1 quart low is OK, 2+ quarts low risks engine damage).

decisions.reason: VS50711 is unscoped across N20 and B48 generations, and exact application for this later X3 article is not established.

sourceEvidence.title: Valve Cover Gasket Oil Leak
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the valve cover gasket. Inspect the valve cover for warping or cracks — if damaged, replace the entire cover assembly. Clean all oil residue from surrounding components. Use a torque wrench to prevent over-tightening which causes cover warping.

decisions.reason: DEP1038 is unscoped across the article's unknown engines and incomplete without the prescribed thermostat.

sourceEvidence.title: Electric Water Pump Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the electric water pump and thermostat as a pair. Bleed the cooling system completely after installation. Keep a close eye on coolant temperature gauge as early detection is key to preventing engine damage from overheating.

decisions.component: E70 rear self-leveling air-supply system (only after EHC diagnosis and VIN confirmation)
decisions.reason: The air-supply assembly is diagnosis- and VIN-conditional, but the current public claim has no enforceable fitment or completed EHC diagnosis gate.

sourceEvidence.title: E70 Rear Air-Supply Unit: Diagnose the Self-Leveling System First
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Read the EHC fault memory and run the applicable BMW ISTA test plan before ordering a compressor. Confirm the vehicle is equipped with rear self-leveling suspension, compare left/right ride height, check system power and wiring, inspect the height-sensor links, and leak-test the air springs, lines, and valve system. Test the air supply only after those checks isolate it. If BMW ETK/AIR selects the E70 air-supply system for the VIN and diagnosis confirms that assembly, replace it with current part 37-20-6-859-714, follow the BMW repair procedure, clear faults, and perform the required ride-height calibration. Do not install a generic compressor or a coil-conversion kit from symptoms alone.

decisions.component: N62/N62TU coolant transfer pipe (only after pressure-test confirmation)
decisions.reason: The N62 transfer pipe is pressure-test- and VIN-conditional, while the current public claim has no machine-enforceable fitment or diagnosis gate.

sourceEvidence.title: E70 N62 Coolant Transfer Pipe Leak (Pressure-Test First)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Pressure-test the cooling system cold and inspect the engine valley and all accessible connections to identify the exact leak before ordering parts. If inspection confirms the N62 transfer pipe and BMW ETK/AIR selects it for the VIN, replace pipe 11-14-1-439-975 with the required seals and one-time-use hardware from the VIN-specific repair diagram. Refill and bleed the cooling system with the specified coolant, repeat the pressure test, and verify stable temperature. Do not automatically replace an N63 pipe, thermostat, or unrelated hoses from this article.

decisions.component: Valve-stem seal repair kits (two required, only after confirmed valve-seal leakage)
decisions.reason: Valve-stem seals are only one possible cause after formal oil-consumption diagnosis, yet the current claim is unscoped and immediately linkable.

sourceEvidence.title: N63 Twin-Turbo V8 Excessive Oil Consumption
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Keep the oil at the correct approved level, inspect for external and turbo/ventilation-system leaks, and have a BMW center or qualified BMW specialist perform the applicable oil-consumption test and diagnostic checks. Ask the dealer to verify VIN-specific eligibility for the early N63 or N63TU1 settlement/service benefits before buying parts. Replace valve-stem seals only when testing and inspection confirm that repair path. The current BMW valve-seal kit is 11-34-0-054-492, which supersedes 11-34-0-039-494; BMW specifies two 16-seal kits for the V8, plus VIN-specific one-time-use gaskets, seals, injector hardware, oil, and filter. Turbo, oil-separator, ventilation-line, or engine replacement is conditional on the corresponding inspection result.

decisions.component: Both N63 timing-chain systems (only after failed BMW ISTA elongation test)
decisions.reason: This is a text-only, no-link warning that explicitly requires the ISTA elongation test and does not expose a retail product.

sourceEvidence.title: Early N63 Timing-Chain Wear Check: ISTA Test Before Repair
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Check the VIN and service history with a BMW center, diagnose stored VANOS/camshaft faults first, and run BMW's ISTA timing-chain elongation test. If the result is 'Timing chain is OK,' do not replace parts on this claim. If it is 'not OK,' BMW SIB 11 16 14 directs replacement of both timing chains under the VIN-specific repair instruction, followed by the required oil/filter service, priming steps, programming, and shorter oil-service interval. A single tensioner 11-31-7-557-741 or a generic Cloyes kit is not the complete repair and must not be presented as what the owner needs. Tow the vehicle rather than driving it when severe mechanical noise, oil-pressure warnings, or loss of timing is present.

decisions.component: M54 valve-cover profile-gasket set (only after leak-source and cover inspection)
decisions.reason: The gasket is conditional on leak-source and cover inspection, but the current public claim has no completed diagnosis gate or enforceable fitment.

sourceEvidence.title: E53 3.0i M54 Valve-Cover Gasket Leak (Confirm the Source)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Clean the engine and trace the highest fresh-oil source before ordering a gasket. If the leak is at the M54 cylinder-head-cover perimeter or spark-plug-well seals, inspect the plastic cover for cracks, warpage, damaged fastener grommets, and crankcase-ventilation faults. Reuse the cover only if it passes inspection, then install VIN/production-confirmed gasket set 11-12-0-030-496 with the BMW-specified grommets and sealant locations and torque sequence. If the cover or another oil circuit is the source, select that separate repair instead.

decisions.component: ATC700 transfer-case exchange servomotor (only after VTG diagnosis and VIN confirmation)
decisions.reason: The ATC700 motor is VIN- and VTG-diagnosis-dependent, while the current public link can render before those conditions are met.

sourceEvidence.title: E70 ATC700 Transfer-Case Positioning Motor (Diagnosis Required)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Read BMW VTG/DSC faults and run the applicable ISTA transfer-case test plan before buying a motor. Confirm tire sizes and wear, battery voltage, wiring, transfer-case type, fluid condition, calibration, and—especially after differential or transfer-case replacement—the VIN-correct front and rear gear ratios. If testing confirms the ATC700 positioning motor and BMW ETK/AIR selects this application for the VIN, current BMW exchange servomotor 27-10-2-449-709 supersedes 27-10-7-568-267. Install the correct classification resistor/hardware supplied or specified for the VIN and perform the required VTG initialization/calibration. A generic gear-only kit is not a universal BMW repair and should not be ordered without opening and confirming the exact motor failure.

decisions.component: BMW DTF-1 transfer-case oil, 1 liter (only after SIB 27 02 20 diagnosis selects oil service)
decisions.reason: DTF-1 service is only selected after the SIB tire, fault, and clutch-deactivation tests; the public claim has no diagnosis gate or vehicle scope.

sourceEvidence.title: G05/F95 Transfer-Case Shudder: Tires and Fluid Diagnosis First
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Follow BMW SIB 27 02 20 in order: verify all four tires for VIN-correct size, brand/application, axle placement, and wear; diagnose any powertrain faults; then use ISTA to temporarily deactivate the transfer-case clutch and road-test the complaint. Only if the shudder disappears with the VTG deactivated does BMW direct an ATX13-X oil change with DTF-1, followed by VTG calibration. The clutch plates can require up to 125 miles after the service to become fully saturated and smooth out. If the symptom remains, continue diagnosis rather than buying an actuator or transfer case. Part numbers for any further repair must be selected by VIN in ETK/AIR.

decisions.component: N62 valve-stem seal kit, 16 seals per bank (quantity 2 required)
partNumbers: MAHLE SS46055 (ShowMeTheParts part key 006471628; N62/N62B48; 16 seals; quantity 2)
decisions.reason: The two-kit valve-seal repair is diagnosis- and VIN-conditional, while the current unscoped public claim can render before confirmation.

sourceEvidence.title: E53 N62 Blue Smoke: Confirm Valve-Stem Seals Before Repair
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Measure oil consumption under consistent conditions, inspect for external leaks and crankcase-ventilation faults, check intake contamination, evaluate spark plugs and cylinders, and have a BMW-capable shop confirm the valve-stem-seal diagnosis. If the N62 seals are confirmed and BMW ETK/AIR selects 11-34-0-029-751 for the VIN, the 32-valve V8 requires two 16-seal kits, one for each bank. Use the BMW repair procedure and special tools, replace only the additional seals and one-time-use hardware identified by the VIN-specific diagram, then verify compression, oil use, and smoke after repair. Oil or an oil filter does not repair hardened valve-stem seals.

decisions.component: VANOS adjustment-unit recall remedy (dealer inspection determines bolts versus adjustment unit)
decisions.reason: This is a recall-first, no-link dealer-remedy card that explicitly says not to buy a VANOS part first.

sourceEvidence.title: VANOS Adjustment-Unit Bolt Recall 23V-707 (E70 Inline-Six)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Enter the VIN in BMW's official recall lookup and have an authorized BMW center complete recall 23V-707 if it is open. BMW's procedure is inspection-dependent: intact affected bolts are replaced; if bolts are loose or broken, the affected VANOS adjustment unit is replaced, and missing fragments must be recovered. The recall repair is free, so do not buy a solenoid or VANOS part first. If the VIN is outside the recall or a fault remains after the remedy, use BMW-capable diagnostics to test oil supply and pressure, wiring, sensors, control solenoids, adjustment units, and mechanical timing before selecting a part. If the engine runs roughly, makes unusual mechanical noise, loses power, or stalls, move out of traffic safely, stop driving, and contact BMW for transport guidance.

decisions.component: N55 electric engine-coolant pump (only after ISTA diagnosis and VIN confirmation)
decisions.reason: The N55 pump is ISTA- and VIN-conditional, but the current public claim lacks an enforceable completed-diagnosis gate.

sourceEvidence.title: E70 xDrive35i N55 Electric Coolant Pump (Fault-Confirmed)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: If the engine-temperature warning appears, stop safely, shut the engine off, and tow the vehicle if normal temperature cannot be confirmed. When cool, check coolant level and leaks, read BMW-specific faults, verify pump power/ground and communication, and run the ISTA coolant-pump activation/test plan. If those tests confirm the pump and BMW ETK/AIR selects 11-51-5-A05-704 for the VIN, replace it using the BMW procedure, select the thermostat separately only if testing or preventive planning justifies it, vacuum-fill or bleed the system as specified, and verify commanded pump operation and stable temperature. Do not use a fixed-mileage rule or this part number for an N52, N63, or F15 without VIN confirmation.

decisions.reason: The unscoped Gates 41236 claim spans both B48 and B58 while the article names different OEM pumps and requires a pump-and-thermostat repair bundle.

sourceEvidence.title: B48/B58 Electric Water Pump & Thermostat Failure - G29 Z4
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Preventative replacement recommended at 60,000 miles. Always replace water pump and thermostat together - they share labor overlap and frequently fail concurrently. B48 sDrive30i: Water pump BMW 11518632586 ($300-$450), Thermostat BMW 11538685978 ($100-$150). B58 M40i: Water pump BMW 11518650986 ($350-$500), Thermostat BMW 11538685978 ($100-$150). Mishimoto offers performance water pump alternatives for B58 with improved impeller design. Replace 3 O-rings between thermostat and pump housing, plus 2 O-rings on coolant tube to head. Must replace water pump mounting bolts (torque-to-yield). Labor: 3-4 hours. FCP Euro lifetime warranty kits available. Also inspect plastic cylinder head coolant outlet adapter - known to shear off causing massive coolant leak.
